blocking_findings.issue: The stanza slug for מִיּוֹדְעֵי does not follow the transliteration rules. JLPTEI-3 lines 145-146 (rule-stanzas.md) say a shva after a long vowel (holam) is sounded as 'e'. That makes יוֹדְעֵי yo-de-ei, so the slug should be 'miyodeei'. The sister poem in the same decision file already applies this rule: לְיוֹדְעָיו → 'leyodeav' (essa_dei_betzedeq). The dagesh in the yod comes from the mem prefix, so not doubling it ('miy', not 'miyy') is correct. Only the dropped sounded shva is wrong. This is a new canonical identity URN, so it should be fixed before it becomes stable.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Rename the slug to 'miyodeei' in both HE and EN together, so HE and EN still match one-to-one, and update the incipit decision record. Alternative: if 'miyodei' is a deliberate spelling, record it in specs/naming/spellings.yaml with the reason.

verdict: Not approved, for one blocking issue. Everything else in the shabbat_poem scope checks out. Both languages have exactly 46 stanzas in the same order, using incipit slugs (no ordinal stanza_N), matched one-to-one between HE and EN. All nine Bible insertions are in the right places: after 30 Ex 19:16, after 32 Ps 47:6 + 98:6, after 34 Isa 27:13, after 36 Ex 19:19, after 38 Ps 81:4-5, after 40 Isa 18:3, after 42 Ex 20:18 (canonical WLC numbering per the evidence), after 44 Ps 150:1-6, and after 46 Zech 9:14 plus the 15 verse-part 'adonai_tzevaot_yagen'. Each stanza scope is closed explicitly before the intro prayer-part. The ק׳/ח׳ speaker rubrics sit outside stanza scope. Chapter, verse and verse-part scopes all close before the next unit, with canonical @n values, and the partial Zech 9:15 is namespaced so it does not claim the whole verse. The CGJ in Jerusalem is preserved, and there are no Biblical accents. The EN Ex 20:18 sic/corr adds only the closing quote, and EN Ps 150 is unquoted, as in the source. Page facsimiles are consistent: HE n293-n305 odd, EN n294-n306 even, and the page breaks fall at matching positions in both languages. Ken Tagen is a separate occurrence in both languages. Blocking: the slug 'miyodei' breaks the sounded-shva-after-holam rule; it should be 'miyodeei', consistent with 'leyodeav'. Once that slug is renamed in both languages, or recorded as a deliberate spelling exception, this scope can be approved. This approval would not cover other groups, code or export.
